Surrogate Formulation for Chance-Constrained DC Optimal Power Flow With
Afﬁne Control Policy
Xingyu Lei , Member , IEEE, Zhifang Y ang , Member , IEEE, Junbo Zhao , Senior Member , IEEE,
Juan Y u , Senior Member , IEEE, and Wenyuan Li , Life Fellow, IEEE
Abstract—In chance-constrained DC optimal power ﬂow (CC-
DCOPF) with afﬁne control policy, the distribution of uncertainty
variables is a function of the decision variable. Existing methods fail
to transform chance constraints into an analytical form, resulting
in computational difﬁculties. This letter proposes a surrogate for-
mulation for CC-DCOPF considering the afﬁne control policy. The
data-driven surrogate model is constructed to identify the mapping
relationship between the afﬁne control variables and the tightening
boundary of chance constraints. This allows us to analytically
reformulate the chance constraints in the presence of non-Gaussian
correlated uncertainties. By leveraging the physical power ﬂow
features, the surrogate model is scaled into a simple single function.
This enables us to use the piecewise linearization technique to ap-
proximate the CC-DCOPF to a mixed-integer linear programming
(MILP) problem. Case studies show that the proposed method leads
to a near-optimal solution with high computational efﬁciency.
Index Terms —DC optimal power ﬂow, chance constraints,
surrogate model, renewable energy, data-driven.
I. I NTRODUCTION
A
S A representative stochastic optimization method,
chance-constrained optimization has been widely used for
uncertainty management in DC optimal power ﬂow (DCOPF)
[1]. For the chance-constrained DC optimal power ﬂow (CC-
DCOPF) problem, existing methods can be generally classiﬁed
into sampling-based methods and distribution-based methods.
In the sampling-based methods, the probabilities of chance con-
straints are estimated by sampling techniques [2], [3]. Because
the optimality is ensured with the detailed modeling of each sce-
nario, the computational burden quickly rises with the number
of scenarios. In the distribution-based methods, the CC-DCOPF
is usually formulated as a deterministic optimization problem
based on speciﬁc probabilistic distribution assumptions [4].
Data-driven nonparametric uncertainty modeling methods, such

address the distribution assumption issues. This is achieved by
modeling the tightening boundary of chance constraints as the
inverse cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) of uncertainty
variables with a pre-determined afﬁne control policy, which is
estimated from a database. An iterative approach is proposed
in [6] to ﬁnd a suitable security parameter to guarantee the
feasibility of the CC-DCOPF problem under a non-Gaussian
uncertainty distribution.
The afﬁne control policy modeled by the automatic generation
control (AGC) participation factors can be used to reﬂect the
adjustment of conventional generators for compensating the
power mismatch caused by uncertainties. However, it brings
a formulation challenge in the CC-DCOPF modeling because
the uncertainty variables, such as transmission power ﬂows and
generation outputs, will be inﬂuenced by the AGC participation
factors. It is difﬁcult to analytically express the inverse CDFs
in the form of the tightening boundary of chance constraints
because the CDFs of uncertainty variables become a function of
the AGC participation factors. To the best of our knowledge,
there is still no solution yet for the analytical expression in
the presence of non-Gaussian uncertainty variables consider-
ing the AGC participation factors. In this letter, a data-driven
method for the CC-DCOPF reformulation with non-Gaussian
uncertainties is developed. Instead of modeling the CDFs, a
data-driven surrogate model is constructed to directly identify
the tightening boundary, which can be used as a function of
AGC participation factors in the CC-DCOPF. Furthermore, the
data-driven surrogate model is scaled into a simple single-
function based on the physical power ﬂow features, avoiding
the high-dimensional mapping relationship which is established
in the learning process from the AGC participation factors to
the tightening boundary of chance constraints. This enables us
not only to build an accurate surrogate model but also to use the
piecewise linearization technique to guarantee the convexity of
the CC-DCOPF problem.

where UM (β) represents the tightening boundary of the speciﬁc
chance constraint, namely uncertainty margin (UM), which is
correlated with βand system uncertainties. Usually, the chance
constraints (2a)–(2d) are hard to be analytically reformulated
in the presence of non-Gaussian correlated uncertainties due
to the lack of closed-form of the UM. In existing methods,
with a pre-determined β, an approximate UM is established by
using the nonparametric modeling method to create the inverse
CDFs of uncertainty variables [5]. Thus, the CC-DCOPF can be
transformed into a linear programming problem. However, βis
a dispatch variable and keeps changing in the optimization pro-
cess. Therefore, it is extremely difﬁcult, not to say impossible,
to build the inverse CDFs under the condition of countiously
changing AGC participation factors.
To address this challenging issue, a data-driven surrogate
model-based CC-DCOPF method is proposed. From a data-
driven perspective, the UM can be regarded as a mapping
function ofβ, which can be approximated using historical data.
Hence, the key idea is to construct a data-driven surrogate model
f: β→UM (β) to obtain the analytical closed-form of UM (β).
Then, by embedding the surrogated UM into (2a)–(2d),t h e
CC-DCOPF with the afﬁne control policy can be solved by an
off-the-shelf solver. It is worth noting that some other methods,
such as the robust optimization, can be also used to handle
various stochastic optimization problems [7]. Different methods
have distinct features and advantages/disadvantages. We only
focus on the chance-constrained approach in this letter.

gence issues. To reduce the number of integer variables in
transmission constraints, a successive constraint identiﬁcation
method is applied to solve the MILP . The successive con-
straint identiﬁcation method is summarized as follows. First,
the CC-DCOPF in the MILP form, including only the active
transmission constraints in the deterministic DC-OPF is solved.
Second, whether the obtained solution satisﬁes all transmission
constraints is checked. Third, the violated transmission con-
straints are added back to the problem, and the MILP is resolved
until the convergence criterion is reached.
IV . NUMERICAL RESULTS
In this section, the proposed method is tested on the IEEE
118-bus system with 5 wind farms. The realistic wind power
data is obtained from Bonneville Power Administration [9].T h e
loads are assumed to follow a Gaussian distribution with stan-
dard deviations equaling 5% of the original loads. Three hundred
training samples are generated for the surrogate modeling. The
simulations are performed on a PC equipped with Intel Core
i7-8700 CPU @ 3.20 GHz 32 GB RAM.
The following methods are compared.
M0: the proposed method;
M1: the sampling-based method proposed in [2];
M2: the improved sampling-based method according to [3]2;
M3: GMM-based method [5] (the AGC participation factors are
ﬁxed according to the maximum outputs of generators).

is compared with two scenarios-based methods (M1 and M2)

Several conclusions can be drawn as follows:
1) Compared with the scenarios-based methods, the pro-
posed method can achieve a near-optimal solution. With
the increasing number of scenarios, M1 and M2 will need
to increase the number of involved integer variables. By
contrast, the proposed method can conveniently handle
this situation because the problem scale of the proposed
method (inﬂuenced by the piecewise linear segments ×
the number of transmission constraints ) does not rely on
the number of scenarios. Meanwhile, the involved integer
variables can be further reduced in each step of the iterative
solution process using the proposed successive constraint
identiﬁcation method.
2) By comparing M1 and M2, we can observe that for the
sampling-based method, the calculation performance can
be greatly improved using proper techniques, like the
constraint screening and the tighten of Big-M value in
[3]. The proposed method presents a different approach
to address this CC-OPF problem using the assistance of
data-driven tools. The implementation is straightforward,
providing a new perspective to solve this problem.
B. Performance With Different Conﬁdence Levels
The proposed method is tested with the conﬁdence levels
ranging from 8% to 15%. The number of uncertainty scenarios
used for both the CC-DCOPF modeling and the max constraint
violation probabilities testing is set to 10000. The results are
shown in Fig. 1. The sampling-based methods presented by M1
and M2 can achieve the optimality given sufﬁcient computa-
tional time, which can be regarded as the benchmark. Here,
the proposed method is compared with the distribution-based
method (M3), as shown in Fig. 1.
The blue line represents the generation cost under different
conﬁdence levels. We can see that the generation costs gradually
decrease as the pre-deﬁned conﬁdence level increases, which
means that lower conﬁdence achieves more conservative solu-
tion results. As can be seen from Fig.1, the GMM-based method
cannot solve the cases with conﬁdence levels ranging under
10% because the AGC participation factors cannot be optimized
by the GMM-based method. Compared with the GMM-based
method (dashed lines in Fig. 1), the proposed method (solid
lines in Fig. 1) can ﬁnd the solution under a stricter conﬁdence
level while having a lower generation cost. This is because the
AGC participation factors optimization provides extra ﬂexibility
to handle uncertainties.
The orange line represents the absolute error of max violation
probability. For the GMM-based method, the absolute error of
max violation probability is relatively large, which comes from
the GMM-based modeling for uncertainties distribution. The
GMM-based method approximates the uncertainty distribution
based on the historical data to obtain the CDFs of uncertainty
variables for CC-DCOPF modeling. The approximate error
leads to the max violation probability diverting from the pre-
deﬁned conﬁdence level. By comparison, the proposed method
(solid lines in Fig. 1) directly constructs the surrogate model of
uncertainty margin by historical data. The uncertainty modeling
error is avoided, achieving a lower absolute error of max viola-
tion probability than the GMM-based methods. It shows better
feasibility for the required conﬁdence level.
V. C ONCLUSION
This letter proposes a data-driven surrogate model based
method for the CC-DCOPF problem considering the afﬁne con-
trol policy. To the best of our knowledge, the proposed method is
the ﬁrst CC-DCOPF method considering the continuous changes
of AGC participation factors in the optimization process without
any uncertainty distribution assumptions. The performance is
justiﬁed in the case studies. The proposed method provides extra
ﬂexibility to handle uncertainties in the CC-DCOPF problem.
